NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI accelerator value chain, functioning as a fabless semiconductor company that designs leading-edge GPUs and networking chips but relies critically on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and HBM memory suppliers like SK Hynix for high-performance stacked memory. On the demand side, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily concentrated among a small number of hyperscale cloud providers — Microsoft, Meta, Google, and Amazon — who collectively account for the majority of data center GPU purchases, creating both massive growth leverage and meaningful customer concentration risk.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, designing its own silicon and software while outsourcing manufacturing to a concentrated network of Asian suppliers and foundries — most critically TSMC for chips and Samsung/LG for displays. On the demand side, Apple sells primarily through its own retail and online channels supplemented by major wireless carriers and retailers, with its high-margin Services segment increasingly dependent on platform relationships such as Google's search revenue sharing agreement.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the pivotal center of the global semiconductor supply chain, acting as the world's dominant pure-play foundry that is almost entirely dependent on a concentrated group of specialized equipment and materials suppliers — most critically ASML for irreplaceable lithography tools — while serving virtually every major fabless chip designer and systems company globally. Its downstream customer base is highly concentrated among a few hyperscaler-driven chip designers such as Apple, NVIDIA, and AMD, making TSMC both strategically indispensable and exposed to demand cycles in consumer electronics, AI infrastructure, and cloud computing.

On the demand side, Micron's fortunes are increasingly tied to AI-driven infrastructure buildout—particularly HBM sales to NVIDIA—alongside secular demand from cloud hyperscalers and mobile OEMs, making its revenue highly sensitive to both equipment availability and end-market capex cycles.

On the downstream side, the company's revenue is primarily driven by Bitcoin spot prices and the sale of mined BTC through exchanges like Coinbase, while its growing AI cloud segment seeks hyperscale and enterprise customers for GPU-as-a-service compute capacity.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo sits at a nascent but strategically critical position in the advanced fission power chain, sourcing high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel and specialized reactor components from a narrow set of domestic nuclear suppliers while targeting large-scale commercial and data center customers hungry for firm, carbon-free power. As a pre-revenue company still awaiting NRC licensing approval for its Aurora powerhouse, its supply chain relationships remain largely contractual or prospective, making fuel access from enrichers like Centrus and government facilitation from the DOE existential dependencies at this stage.
